text.text: Sales, jobs, money, team and goals in one place. Start with the pipeline, then check this week's tasks and unpaid invoices.
Monday: huddle, set priorities, assign proofs
Wednesday: chase proposals older than a week
Friday: send invoices for finished jobs and log expenses
If a deal has not moved in two weeks, it is either Lost or needs a call.

A small business runs on a handful of habits done on the same day every week. The checklist above is a starting point; change the days to match your own work, but keep them fixed so that everyone knows when the pipeline gets cleaned and when the invoices go out.
Open deals with a close date in the past: move them or mark them lost.
Overdue invoices: one call or message each, the same week they turn overdue.
Tasks due this week: anything not assigned gets an owner on Monday.
Every record links to the next one: a contact has deals, a won deal becomes a job, a job has tasks and an invoice. Fill the links in and the totals work themselves out.
Add a contact, then log a deal against them.
When a deal is Won, create a project and tasks.
Assign tasks to teammates and track due dates.
Invoice when the project is done and mark it Paid when money arrives.
Log expenses as they happen so the month-end is easy.
Contact: Won value, Open deal value, Billed, Paid, Balance owed and Spent with them.
Job: tasks done, tasks left and progress.
Invoice: days late, counted from the due date.
Goal: progress and what is left to go.
Twenty minutes at the end of the month saves hours at tax time. Work down the list in order; each step makes the next one easier.
Every receipt entered as an expense

Open the Expenses table on its This month view, then the Paid this month view on invoices. Compare the two totals in your head: are you moving in the direction you planned? Write one sentence about it in the Goals row for revenue.
